battle.name: 古提王朝的滅亡
battle.theater: 美索不達米亞中部與扎格羅斯山麓
battle.brief: 公元前二一一九年，扎格羅斯山麓的古提人自阿卡德覆亡後盤踞蘇美爾已近半世紀，烏爾的祭司烏圖亨伽爾在南部城邦起兵，沿幼發拉底北上，於尼普爾與烏萊河畔擊潰古提軍，古提王朝就此覆亡。本卡那件早王朝的埃及長矛，正是同代束柄銅矛的同型兵器，攻城與野戰皆靠它立陣。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 交戰的兩方，是扎格羅斯山麓的古提人聯盟，與南部美索不達米亞的蘇美爾城邦聯軍。古提一方並非國家，而是沒有留下文字、沒有留下正式王號的高地部族聯盟：其戰力集中在山口的隘路、牧場與商道驛站，作戰以步兵為主，配短弓、投石索與銅斧，車兵極少，運輸依靠馱畜；指揮依靠首領與各部族長的號令，今日所存的同期文獻幾乎沒有留下任何古提將領的名字，唯一常被引用的名號是部分抄本所記的古提王「提里甘」，其拼寫與出處都未有一致的考定。蘇美爾一方則是烏爾、尼普爾、烏魯克、埃里都、拉加什等城邦臨時拼成的聯軍，形式上由烏圖亨伽爾以烏爾城最高祭司兼「王」的身分號召，實際上各城按自己的老規矩出錢、出地、出船：步兵來自各城的鄉村徵召，貴族與城衛提供戰車，工匠與船夫維持河運，祭司集團則在神廟層面提供統治的合法性。當時並沒有常備軍，常備兵與中央稅制是這場勝利之後由其子舒爾吉與其孫烏爾納瑪才建立起來的。古提人佔領時期，蘇美爾各城唯一還完整運作的機構，是各城神廟的祭司團體與泥板檔案；也正是這套機構記下了起義的經過，把古提的佔領寫成《蘇美爾王表》裏一段「無王之時」的空白。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were a confederation of Gutian highlanders from the Zagros foothills and a coalition of the Sumerian city-states of southern Mesopotamia. The Gutian side was not a state at all but a loose tribal confederation that left behind neither writing nor formal royal titulature: its military strength lay in the mountain passes, the pastures and the caravan stations of the trade routes; it fought mainly on foot, armed with short bows, slings and copper axes, with very few wagons and pack animals for transport; command rested with the war-leader and the clan chiefs. Almost no Gutian commander is named in the texts that survive from the period; the only name often quoted is that of a Gutian ruler called Tirigan in a few manuscripts, and both its spelling and its source remain unsettled. The Sumerian side was an improvised coalition of Ur, Nippur, Uruk, Eridu, Lagash and the other cities, formally called out by Utu-hengal in his capacity as chief priest of the city of Ur and as 'king', but in practice each city supplied money, land and boats according to its own custom: infantry came from the village levies of the individual cities, nobles and city guards provided the chariots, craftsmen and boatmen kept river transport running, and the priestly colleges supplied legitimacy at the level of the temples. There was no standing army as yet; the regular army and the central tax system were created only after this victory by his son Shulgi and his grandson Ur-Nammu. During the Gutian occupation the only institutions in the Sumerian cities that still functioned in full were the priestly colleges and the clay-tablet archives of the temples; and it was precisely those institutions that recorded the rising, turning the Gutian occupation into the blank stretch of 'a time with no kings' in the Sumerian King List.
people: 主線只有一個人：烏圖亨伽爾（Utu-hengal）。他的名字意為「偉大的烏圖」，是蘇美爾王名中的神聖名號，本身便宣告他以烏爾的烏圖神祭司身分行使王權；據《蘇美爾王表》，他的父親是烏巴（U-bar）。他把南部城邦的武裝起義整合成聯軍，擊敗古提軍，在位七年，隨後把王位移給其子舒爾吉（Shulgi）；其子舒爾吉據同一王表在位九年，孫子烏爾納瑪（Ur-Nammu）十八年，烏爾第三王朝由此開端。古提一方的主帥姓名，今存同期文本幾乎全部缺漏；部分晚期抄本與現代辭書把古提之王記作「提里甘」，本文姑存其名而不作定論——可以確定的只是：這位古提領袖統率的是一個聯盟，盟內各部族各有自己的首領，戰敗時並非一體崩潰，而是分批退回山地。文字方面需要留意的，是記錄這場戰爭的兩份關鍵文本都不是當年的創作：其一是一篇巴比倫時代的雙語編年史（今稱《韋德納編年史》或《拉薩編年史》），用極簡的筆法記下「烏萊河之戰」與古提人的退走，並提到蘇美爾人推烏圖亨伽爾為王；其二是出土於尼普爾的數學泥板，學界編號 YBC 7289，題為「烏圖亨伽爾之捷」，以算式把「尼普爾之戰」的紀日與「烏萊河之戰」的年號寫下來。此外還有尼普爾寧吉爾蘇神廟出土的烏圖亨伽爾奠基銘板，以及其子舒爾吉的紀功銘文，後者追述父親「使蘇美爾的百姓得以存活、把土地重新理順」。
peopleEn: The central figure is a single man: Utu-hengal. His name means 'Utu the great' and is a divine name in Sumerian royal nomenclature, itself an assertion that he exercised kingship in the capacity of chief priest of Utu at Ur; according to the Sumerian King List his father was U-bar. He drew the armed risings of the southern cities together into a coalition, beat the Gutian army, and reigned seven years before passing the kingship to his son Shulgi; the same list gives Shulgi nine years and Shulgi's son Ur-Nammu eighteen, and with them the Third Dynasty of Ur begins. The name of the Gutian commander-in-chief is missing from almost all the contemporary texts that survive; a few later manuscripts and modern dictionaries record the name of a Gutian king as 'Tirigan', and this account keeps the name without endorsing it — what can be established is only that the Gutian leader commanded a confederation whose clans each had their own chiefs, and that the alliance did not collapse in one piece after the defeat but returned to the mountains in separate bands. Two points about the written record must be kept in mind: neither of the two key texts describing this war was composed at the time. The first is a bilingual Old Babylonian chronicle (now called the Weidner Chronicle or the Larsa Chronicle), which in very terse lines records the 'battle of the River Ulai' and the withdrawal of the Gutians, and notes that the Sumerians made Utu-hengal their king; the second is a mathematical clay tablet found at Nippur, catalogued by scholars as YBC 7289 and titled 'The Victory of Utu-hengal', which writes down in arithmetic form the day-count of the 'battle of Nippur' and the year-name of the 'battle of the River Ulai'. There is also Utu-hengal's foundation plaque from the temple of Ningirsu at Nippur, and the victory inscription of his son Shulgi, which looks back on a father who 'saved the people of Sumer and set the land in order again'.
kits: 本卡兵器是埃及長矛：早王朝時期把銅或青銅矛頭套在木杆上的步戰長矛，埃及人用它守住城垣缺口，也在異族入主時用來收復失地。要說明的是，前二一一九年的這場戰爭裡沒有埃及人：現存文本與考古都沒有顯示埃及軍隊曾參與美索不達米亞的戰事，埃及與兩河流域的聯繫，那時主要經由比布魯斯（Byblos）轉手的木材、銅與「馬干」（即阿曼的銅）貿易，以及蘇美爾商人通往阿卡德以東的商路，而不是軍隊。所以本卡兵器在這場戰爭中的位置，是一個技術坐標：前四王朝的埃及與蘇美爾同屬青銅時代早期的同一武器系統，兩地的步兵骨幹都是束柄銅矛加斧，盾面同樣以皮條與銅釦加固。矛頭形制也相近——早王朝的葉形寬刃銅矛頭，錐形莖插入木杆再以皮條或麻纖捆紮；依出土矛頭的尺寸與握持比例推估，全槍長約二公尺上下，介乎二至二點五公尺之間。蘇美爾方面實際使用的裝備包括：銅矛頭（烏爾王陵早王朝墓葬出土的成組矛頭是現存最完整的標本）、銅斧、短匕首、石與骨製箭鏃、複合弓、投石索、長方形與圓形大盾，以及蘑菇形與圓盤形的「標準」旗幟；車兵用野驢挽具拉動的四輪戰車，車上一名御者、一名持矛或斧的戰鬥員，馬匹要到前十八世紀才傳入兩河流域。攻城方面沒有留下直接證據顯示當時已有撞槌或攻城塔，最可能的方式是沿城牆斜坡段、缺口與水門攀援，並以投石與火攻消耗守軍。陸上補給靠牛車，水上靠幼發拉底與卡爾帕塔斯河的蘆葦船與河船。
kitsEn: The card shows the Egyptian spear: an infantry spear of the Early Dynastic period, a copper or bronze head socketed onto a wooden shaft, used by the Egyptians to hold the gaps in their city walls and later to win back lost land. It should be said plainly that there were no Egyptians in the war of 2119 BC: neither the texts nor the archaeology show an Egyptian army taking part in a Mesopotamian war, and the connections between Egypt and Mesopotamia at that time ran through the timber, copper and 'Magan' (Omanite copper) trade handled by Byblos and through the Sumerian merchant routes running east of Akkad, not through armies. The position of this weapon in the war is therefore that of a technical coordinate: Egypt's Fourth Dynasty and Sumer belonged to the same early Bronze Age arms system, and in both places the backbone of the infantry was the socketed copper spear and axe, with shields reinforced by leather thongs and copper studs. The head forms are comparable as well — the leaf-shaped, broad-bladed copper head of the Early Dynastic period, its tang inserted into a wooden shaft and then bound with leather thongs or hemp cord; judging from the dimensions of excavated heads and the proportions of the grip, the full spear stood at about two metres, somewhere between two and two and a half metres. On the Sumerian side the equipment actually in use included copper spearheads (the sets of Early Dynastic spearheads from the royal cemetery at Ur are the most complete surviving examples), copper axes, short daggers, stone and bone arrowheads, composite bows, slings, large rectangular and round shields, and standard-bearing emblems in mushroom and disc form; the chariots were four-wheeled vehicles drawn by donkeys in onager harness, carrying a driver and a fighting man with spear or axe, since horses did not reach Mesopotamia until the eighteenth century BC. There is no direct evidence for battering rams or siege towers at this date; the likeliest methods were to climb the sloping stretches of wall, the breaches and the water gates, and to wear the defenders down with sling-stones and fire. Landward supply was by ox cart, waterward by reed boats and river craft on the Euphrates and the Karpatas.
tactics: 這場戰爭的樣式，是一次以城市為支點的起義加一次決定性的會戰。古提人的戰法沿襲其高原習性：成隊沿扎格羅斯的谷道下行，控制山口的隘路、牧場與驛站，以步兵快速襲擾邊境村落，奪取牲畜與穀物，再以徵稅的名義向南方城邦索取財貨；他們不佔平原的田地，只取其產出，因此每一次城邦的抵抗都不必先攻城。蘇美爾聯軍的第一步，是奪回南部的河道與收成——只要掌握灌溉渠系與冬穀，聯軍就能供養自己，不必依賴古提人留下的稅糧；第二步是沿幼發拉底北上，逐個奪取中游渡口，把古提人的補給線與牧場切斷，逼其離開熟悉的山地。《韋德納編年史》的殘句透露了這個次序：敵人渡過幼發拉底，兩軍相遇，而「烏萊河之戰」是其中的關鍵；烏萊河一般認為即今伊朗境內的卡爾帕塔斯河。會戰的樣式上，蘇美爾步兵依《標準》與《禿鷹石碑》所示，排成密集的長矛方陣，前排以大盾護身，長矛從盾縫中伸出；車兵擔任衝鋒與追擊，用野驢拉的四輪車撞散敵陣，再以車上的矛與斧追擊潰兵。戰車在這個年代仍是一種貴重工具，數量有限，多配給城邦貴族。相對地，古提步兵在開闊平原上並不佔優——平原正是蘇美爾方陣與車隊最能發揮的地形——所以古提人一旦戰敗便整批退回山區，以游擊與斷糧應對追擊，而不是留下屍位給對方追殺；這正是蘇美爾人在戰術上無法一次解決古提人的原因。攻城戰的具體細節今存材料幾乎空白，可以確定的只是：古提方面的據點倚山而築，蘇美爾聯軍必須靠近日間行軍把攻城器械帶到城下；這也是這場戰爭留下文字最少、卻留下制度最多的一場。
tacticsEn: The shape of this war was a rising organised from the cities, followed by one decisive engagement. The Gutians fought in the manner of their highlands: columns came down the valleys of the Zagros, holding the passes, the pastures and the caravan stations, and their infantry struck quickly at border villages to take livestock and grain, then demanded goods from the southern cities in the form of tribute; they did not occupy the fields of the plain but only their yield, and for that reason no Sumerian resistance ever had to begin with a siege. The first step of the Sumerian coalition was to take back the southern waterways and the harvest — control of the irrigation canals and the winter grain meant the coalition could feed itself without relying on the tribute the Gutians had left behind. The second step was to march north along the Euphrates, taking the middle-course crossings one by one and cutting the Gutians off from their supply lines and pastures, to force them away from the highland terrain they knew. The surviving lines of the Weidner Chronicle hint at this sequence: the enemy crossed the Euphrates, the two armies met, and the 'battle of the River Ulai' was the hinge of the whole thing; the Ulai is generally identified with the modern Karpatas river in Iran. In the battle itself, the Sumerian infantry, as shown on the Standard of Ur and the Stele of the Vultures, formed a dense line of spearmen with large shields in front and spear-points projecting between them; the chariots handled the charge and the pursuit, the four-wheeled donkey-drawn cars breaking the enemy order and then the crew finishing off the fugitives with spear and axe. At this date a chariot was still a costly machine, few in number and mostly in the hands of city aristocrats. By contrast the Gutian infantry were not at their best on the open plain, which was exactly the ground on which the Sumerian phalanx and the chariots fought best; so when the Gutians were beaten they withdrew in whole groups into the mountains and answered pursuit with harassment and cutting of supplies rather than standing and being destroyed. That is why the Sumerians could not finish the Gutians off in one stroke. The details of the siege operations have almost wholly vanished from the record; all that can be said with certainty is that the Gutian strongholds were built against the mountainside and that the Sumerian coalition had to bring its equipment close to the walls by day marching. It is one of the strangest of the ancient wars: almost no tactical text, and yet the institutions it produced.
data: 可以核對的數字大致如下。年代上，阿卡德王朝在通行中年代下崩潰於約前二一五四年（另說前二一五〇年），古提人乘勢取得蘇美爾王權；烏圖亨伽爾在位七年，舒爾吉九年，烏爾納瑪十八年（《蘇美爾王表》），把古提王朝的覆亡定位在前二一一九年前後，即中年代體系。地理上，烏爾在北緯三〇·九六度、東經四六·一〇度，尼普爾在北緯三二·〇四度、東經四四·二五度，兩城沿河約一百五十公里；尼普爾到扎格羅斯山麓的古提山區（今日伊拉克庫爾德斯坦的基爾庫克與拉尼亞平原一帶）約三百至四百公里；烏萊河一般認為即卡爾帕塔斯河，在今伊朗境內，離尼普爾約二百公里。兵器復原上，早王朝葉形銅矛頭長約二〇至三〇公分，全槍長約二至二點五公尺。出土文本方面，YBC 7289 是以算式記下「尼普爾之戰」紀日與「烏萊河之戰」年號的數學泥板，記的是日期與序數，並沒有留下交戰雙方的兵馬數目；古提時期與起義年代的行政泥板極為稀少，兩軍兵力、戰損人數、圍城或追擊的日數，都沒有可靠計數，編年史只說戰事「長久」。可以反向印證的，是蘇美爾在重建王權之後的行政產量急增：烏爾第三王朝時期估計出土的行政泥板約十二萬片，二〇一六年清點約六萬四千五百片得到科學出版，其中吉爾蘇與烏瑪兩地就佔了一半。交通方面，在馬匹傳入之前，兩河流域的車全部由野驢或牛挽拉。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked run as follows. In dating, the Akkadian dynasty collapsed in the standard Middle Chronology at about 2154 BC (2150 BC on an alternative reckoning), and the Gutians took the kingship of Sumer in its wake; Utu-hengal reigned seven years, Shulgi nine and Ur-Nammu eighteen (Sumerian King List), which places the fall of the Gutian dynasty at about 2119 BC within the Middle Chronology system. In geography, Ur lies at 30.96° N, 46.10° E and Nippur at 32.04° N, 44.25° E, about 150 kilometres apart along the river; Nippur lies roughly 300 to 400 kilometres from the Gutian highlands of the Zagros (in modern Iraqi Kurdistan, around Kirkuk and the Rania plain); the Ulai is generally identified with the Karpatas river, now in Iran, some 200 kilometres from Nippur. For the weapon, Early Dynastic leaf-shaped copper spearheads run from about 20 to 30 centimetres, giving a full spear of roughly two to two and a half metres. Among the excavated texts, YBC 7289 is a mathematical tablet that records in figures the day-count of the 'battle of Nippur' and the year-name of the 'battle of the River Ulai'; what it preserves is dates and numbers, not the strength of the armies on either side. Administrative tablets from the Gutian period and from the years of the rising are extremely scarce, and there is no reliable count of the troops engaged, of casualties, or of the length of any siege or pursuit; the chronicle says only that the fighting was 'long'. What can be argued in the other direction is the administrative output that followed the restoration of kingship: something like 120,000 administrative tablets are estimated to have been excavated from the Third Dynasty of Ur, of which about 64,500 had been scientifically published as of 2016, with Girsu and Umma alone accounting for half of them. On transport, before the horse arrived, every cart in Mesopotamia was pulled by a donkey or an ox.
cause: 把這場起義拆開看，是四層原因疊在一起。第一層是結構性的：古提人沒有自己的文字與行政傳統——他們的語言至今未能解讀——佔領蘇美爾之後，只能靠徵收、掠奪與控制商道維持，這套辦法可以支撐幾十年，卻無法把平原的灌溉農業與城市手工業重新編排起來；阿卡德時期已經很發達的冶銅、船運與長途商路在古提時期中斷，《蘇美爾王表》出現「無王之時」，大型工程停擺，幾代人之間，蘇美爾的城市在規模與技術上都退步了。第二層是古提統治的內在脆弱：他們是部族聯盟而非國家，佔領之後各部便散去高原牧場，只留下分管的據點與徵稅的隊伍，因此蘇美爾任何一次像樣的武裝起義，都能得到響應，而統治的中樞一旦在會戰中崩潰，就沒有任何力量可以重建秩序。第三層是蘇美爾方面的載體：神廟的祭司團體與城市的鄉村民兵——青壯年平日耕作，戰時拿起銅矛與大盾列陣，這批人正是《標準》與《禿鷹石碑》所刻的那種持矛步行者；祭司集團則提供「王權來自神授」的說法，給烏圖亨伽爾的起義以正當性。第四層是導火線：具體的年份與細節，今存文本只留下結論性的記載，最可能的直接誘因是一次對南部城邦的徵收或入城式掠奪激起了武裝抵抗，而烏圖亨伽爾在烏爾的號召把零散的抵抗變成聯軍。同一時期，埃及也走進第一中間期的崩解：舊王國的中央權威瓦解，赫拉克利奧波利斯與底比斯兩方對峙，兩地民兵同樣靠束柄銅矛守住城垣——這是本卡那件埃及長矛在時間上真正對應的位置。
causeEn: Taken apart, this rising rests on four layers of cause. The first is structural: the Gutians had no writing of their own and no administrative tradition — their language has still not been deciphered — so after the conquest of Sumer they could maintain themselves only through tribute, plunder and control of the trade routes. That system could hold for decades, but it could never set the plain's irrigation agriculture and urban handicrafts in order again. The bronze metallurgy, shipping and long-distance trade that had already flourished under Akkad broke down during the Gutian period; the Sumerian King List opens a stretch of 'a time with no kings', monumental building stopped, and over several generations the Sumerian cities shrank in size and fell back in technique. The second layer is the inherent fragility of Gutian rule: they were a tribal confederation rather than a state, and once the conquest was made the clans dispersed to their highland pastures, leaving behind only scattered garrisons and tax-collecting bands. Any armed rising in Sumer of any seriousness therefore drew a response, and once the centre of that rule collapsed in a pitched battle, no force remained able to rebuild the order. The third layer is the vehicle on the Sumerian side: the priestly colleges of the temples and the village militia — the young men who ploughed by day and took up the copper spear and the great shield in time of war, the same spearmen in foot that the Standard of Ur and the Stele of the Vultures depict; and the priestly colleges supplied the doctrine that kingship is a gift of the gods, which gave Utu-hengal's rising its legitimacy. The fourth layer is the trigger: of the precise year and circumstances only a conclusory account survives, and the most likely immediate occasion was a collection of tribute or a raid on a southern city that provoked armed resistance, which Utu-hengal's call at Ur turned from scattered resistance into a coalition. At the same time Egypt was entering the collapse of the First Intermediate Period: the central authority of the Old Kingdom dissolved, Herakleopolis and Thebes faced each other, and the militia on both sides held their city walls with the same socketed copper spears. That is where the Egyptian spear on this card truly belongs in time.
impact: 對蘇美爾世界，這場勝利是一條時代分界線。首先是王權性質的改變：烏圖亨伽爾以神廟祭司兼國王的雙重身分開國，開啟了烏爾第三王朝，也開啟了「王的第一政績是重建神廟」這個傳統；其子舒爾吉在位九年，把聯軍改造成國家——設立常備兵、頒布現存最早的《烏爾納瑪法典》、修築城牆與北面的長城抵擋阿摩利特、統一度量衡、設立尼普爾的書吏之家培育抄寫員；其孫烏爾納瑪更把神廟經濟、稅制與常備軍同時制度化，這三樣東西後來成為古巴比倫與亞述的模板，兩河流域由此進入一段延續近三個世紀的制度成熟期。其次是史料的意義：古提時期那段「無王之時」在蘇美爾人的記憶中被永久固定為蠻族入侵的黑暗年代，《阿卡德之詛》把古提人寫成不會說人話、吃生肉的山地人；於是「把王權從高山人手中取回」成為蘇美爾王統敘事的起點，並且一路被伊辛王朝為自身合法性編纂《蘇美爾王表》時反覆引用。第三，古提人並沒有消失：烏爾第三王朝最終仍是在約前二〇〇四年，被另一波古提人與埃蘭聯軍攻滅的——所以前二一一九年不是古提人的終點，而是蘇美爾王權一次短暫而關鍵的復辟。
impactEn: For the Sumerian world this victory is a dividing line. First, the nature of kingship changed: Utu-hengal founded a dynasty in the double capacity of temple priest and king, opening the Third Dynasty of Ur and the tradition that a king's first duty is to rebuild the temples. His son Shulgi reigned nine years and turned the coalition into a state — establishing a standing army, issuing the earliest surviving law code, that of Ur-Nammu, building city walls and a northern frontier wall against the Amorites, standardising weights and measures, and founding the 'house of the scribes' at Nippur to train copyists. His grandson Ur-Nammu institutionalised the temple economy, the taxation system and the standing army at once, and those three instruments later became the model for Babylonia and Assyria; Mesopotamia thus entered a period of institutional maturity that ran for close to three centuries. Second, the meaning of the sources: the Gutian stretch of 'a time with no kings' was permanently fixed in Sumerian memory as a dark age of barbarian invasion, and the Curse of Akkad describes the Gutians as mountaineers who spoke no intelligible tongue and ate raw flesh. 'Taking back the kingship from the highlanders' thus became the starting point of the Sumerian royal narrative, and it was cited over and over as the Isin dynasty compiled the Sumerian King List to justify its own legitimacy. Third, the Gutians did not disappear: the Third Dynasty of Ur was ultimately destroyed in about 2004 BC by another wave of Gutians allied with Elam. So 2119 BC was not the end of the Gutians, but a short and decisive restoration of Sumerian kingship.
result: 結果是古提王朝的崩潰與蘇美爾王權的恢復。前二一一九年前後，烏圖亨伽爾率南部城邦聯軍沿幼發拉底北上，奪回中游渡口，在尼普爾與烏萊河畔同古提主力會戰而勝；古提聯盟當場瓦解，首領與部眾分批退回扎格羅斯山麓，蘇美爾諸城取得數十年的喘息，《蘇美爾王表》記烏圖亨伽爾在位七年，其子舒爾吉在位九年，烏爾第三王朝自此開篇。舊秩序並未完全復原：古提時期被破壞的神廟、淤塞的灌溉渠與空掉的城市，需要整整三代君主才能重新編排，谷物產量與城市人口要再過一百年才回到阿卡德時期的水準；而古提人的影子很快就回來了——約前二〇〇四年，烏爾第三王朝在埃蘭與古提聯軍手下覆滅，蘇美爾再度失去王權，直到前十八世紀才由古巴比倫完成統一。因此這場戰爭的真正落點，不是古提人的消失，而是蘇美爾人第一次證明：城邦聯軍加上一位有神廟背景的首領，能把高原部族聯盟逐回山地，並把「王」從一位占領者的頭銜，重新變成一種可以延續的制度。
resultEn: The result was the collapse of the Gutian dynasty and the restoration of kingship in Sumer. Around 2119 BC, Utu-hengal led the coalition of the southern cities north along the Euphrates, retook the middle-course crossings, and won a pitched battle against the main Gutian force at Nippur and by the River Ulai. The Gutian confederation came apart on the spot, its leaders and their clans withdrawing in separate groups into the Zagros highlands, and the Sumerian cities gained decades of breathing space; the Sumerian King List gives Utu-hengal seven years, his son Shulgi nine, and with them the Third Dynasty of Ur opens. The old order was not fully restored: the temples destroyed during the Gutian period, the silted-up canals and the emptied cities took three whole generations of rulers to set in order again, and grain output and urban population needed another century to reach the levels of Akkadian times. The shadow of the Gutians also returned quickly — in about 2004 BC the Third Dynasty of Ur was overthrown by an Elamite and Gutian coalition, and Sumer lost its kingship again until Old Babylon completed the unification in the eighteenth century BC. The real outcome of this war, then, was not the disappearance of the Gutians; it was the first demonstration, by the Sumerians, that a coalition of cities under a leader with a temple pedigree could drive a highland tribal confederation back into the mountains and turn 'king' from the title of an occupier into an institution capable of continuity.
